channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: US President Donald Trump to hold Iran talks with Gulf leaders next week — Reuters
item.description: US President Donald Trump is expected ‌to meet Gulf leaders on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next Tuesday to discuss the next steps in the Iran war, Reuters reported on Wednesday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar remains weak below 0.5750 despite better-than-expected GDP data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair falls to near 0.5725 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under selling pressure against the US Dollar (USD) despite the upbeat New Zealand economic data. The US Initial Jobless Claims data is due later on Thursday.

item.title: Gold falls to near $4,250 after Fed delivers rate hike
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers to around $4,265 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal extends its downside after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) raises interest rates and signals another rate increase is likely this year.

item.title: 0.2%: New Zealand’s Gross Domestic Product grows more than expected in Q2
item.description: New Zealand's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 0.2% QoQ in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026, compared with a 0.9% expansion in the first quarter (revised from 0.8%), Statistics New Zealand showed on Thursday. This reading came in stronger than the expectation of a rise of 0.1%.

item.title: The Pound drops below its long-run average as the Fed's rate passes Britain's
item.description: The Fed raised rates by a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday, the first hike since 2023, and the vote was 12-0. The middle of the new range is 3.875%, which puts US rates above the UK's 3.75% for the first time this year.

item.title: The Euro's losing streak runs on as the Fed matches the ECB's rate hike
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its deposit rate to 2.50% on September 10, and the Euro has fallen every session since. The Fed raised its own rate to 3.75-4.00% on Wednesday, by the same quarter point, and the day's drop was the biggest of the run.

item.title: The Japanese Yen gives back more of its rally as the Fed raises rates
item.description: The Bank of Japan meets on Friday, and the market has a quarter-point hike to 1.25% priced at 100%. The Yen has been falling anyway. USD/JPY is up three sessions in a row, Wednesday's gain was the biggest of the three, and the pair is trading just under 156.50 after the Fed's hike to 3.75-4.00%.

item.title: New Zealand GDP in the barrel with the Kiwi at July lows
item.description: New Zealand reports second-quarter growth later on Wednesday, or early on Thursday depending on where you are relative to the international date line, and the forecast is 0.1% for the quarter, down from 0.8% in the first three months of the year.

item.title: Trump demands 1% rates hours after the Fed raised them
item.description: Trump posted on Wednesday that US rates should be 1% or less and that the country has the strongest credit anywhere. He also wrote that cutting off trade with every nation the US runs a deficit with would earn at least $1.5 trillion a year.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar sinks toward its July low after the Fed hikes
item.description: NZD/USD has dropped in six straight sessions. The run started near 0.5900 on September 8, went through both long-run averages near 0.5850 early in the run, and the last three sessions have been the biggest of the lot.

item.title: The Australian Dollar continues to slide as the Fed enters hike country
item.description: Australia's central bank pays more than the Federal Reserve (Fed) does. The cash rate is 4.35%, the Fed's new range is 3.75-4.00% after Wednesday's quarter-point hike, and most of the big Australian banks expect the RBA to raise again before the end of the year, and none of that has helped.

item.title: US Federal Reserve sends Gold to fresh one-month lows
item.description: Spot Gold (XAU/USD) is closing Wednesday with losses, trading around $4,250 after hitting an intraday high of $4,366.

item.title: The Euro breaks lower once the Fed raises rates
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades just under 1.1500 against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, through the pair of long-run averages that had held it up since early August.

item.title: The Pound sinks as the Fed overtakes the BoE
item.description: The Pound trades just under 1.3400, 91 pips lower and down 0.68%. The Fed took its rate to 3.75-4.00% and, measured at the midpoint of the new range, American money now pays more than British money for the first time this year.

item.title: Fed rate hike bolsters US Dollar Index above 100.00
item.description: The Dollar Index broke above 100.00, back above both of its long-run averages. The quarter-point that took the Fed to 3.75-4.00% was fully priced and worth nothing on its own.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar slips to a summer low on the Fed's rate hike
item.description: The Loonie trades at its weakest since early August, with USD/CAD just under 1.4000 after a 71-pip rise and a 0.51% gain. The Fed raised its rate a quarter-point to 3.75-4.00% and the Bank of Canada did not, which takes the distance between them from 1.375 points to 1.625.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average slides behind a Federal Reserve hike
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades just above 51,500 on Wednesday, down 576 points and 1.11%, its worst session of the month.

item.title: Silver slides as hawkish Fed lifts US Dollar and Treasury yields
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades under pressure on Wednesday as a stronger US Dollar (USD) and rising US Treasury yields weigh on the non-yielding metal following the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decision. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $62.68, down 1.56% on the day.

item.title: Forex Today: Investors now look at the BoE
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has navigated a positive range on Wednesday, gathering extra pace after the Federal Reserve (Fed) hiked its Fed Funds Target Rate (FFTR) by a quarter percentage point, as widely anticipated.

item.title: Federal Reserve Chair Warsh: Inflation trends were not passing the test
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh is holding a press conference following the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decision to raise the Funds Target Range to 3.75%–4.00%, as expected.

item.title: Fed raises 2026 interest rate forecast to 4.1%, lifts PCE inflation projections
item.description: The Federal Reserve's (Fed) latest dot plot projections, released by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Wednesday, show policymakers now expect interest rates to stand at 4.1% by the end of 2026, up from 3.8% in June.

item.title: Australian Dollar slides below 0.7100 as Warsh strikes hawkish tone
item.description: AUD/USD extends losses on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised interest rates and released a hawkish set of policy projections. The pair slides more than 20 pips in the immediate reaction and trades around 0.7093 at the time of writing.

item.title: Fed’s Warsh: Decision today was the right decision
item.description: This section below was published at 18:00 GMT to cover the Federal Reserve's policy decisions and the immediate market reaction.

item.title: WTI holds near daily low as Fed decision draws muted reaction
item.description: Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil holds near its daily low on Wednesday, showing little immediate reaction to the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, WTI trades around $97.50 per barrel, down roughly 3.3% on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as US Federal Reserve delivers
item.description: The USD/JPY pair trades at fresh weekly highs in the 155.50 price zone after the United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) delivered the expected 25 basis point (bps) interest rate hike. The US Dollar (USD) resumed its weekly advance with the headlines, following a pause ahead of the announcement.

item.title: Federal Reserve hawkish hike sent Gold price lower
item.description: The United States (US) Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announced a 25 basis-point (bps) interest rate hike following its two-day meeting, pushing the US Dollar (USD) firmly up against most major rivals. With this decision, the Funds Target Range (FFTR) stands floating in the 3.75%–4.00% range.

item.title: The Fed hikes to 4% as the 10-year yield toys with 5%
item.description: The Fed has raised its rate to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023 and its first move since the cut in December 2025. The rate it controls is the overnight one. Everything further out is set by people buying and selling bonds, and they have been selling.

item.title: WTI pulls back below $100 as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore Oil flows
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil falls on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia steps up efforts to restore flows through its East-West pipeline, which was damaged by a drone attack last week.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar steadies as markets await Fed decision
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5755 at the time of writing on Wednesday, virtually unchanged on the day after rebounding from an over two-month low at 0.5737.

item.title: Gold consolidates gains as traders brace for Fed interest rate decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates gains on Wednesday after rebounding during Asian trading hours, supported by a modest pullback in Oil prices and US Treasury yields.
